title: Fragments and Run-ons

explanation.en: A fragment lacks a complete main clause. A run-on joins independent sentences incorrectly. Use appropriate punctuation and connectors.
explanation.taglish: Fragment ay kulang na sentence. Run-on ay dalawang complete ideas na mali ang pagkakadugtong. Halimbawa: I finished the report, and I sent it.
explanation.fil: Ang fragment ay kulang na pangungusap. Ang run-on ay dalawang buong ideyang hindi maayos ang pagkakadugtong.

examples: I finished the report, and I sent it.
Because it was late, we went home.

exercises.explanation: A dependent clause by itself may leave an incomplete thought. Correct answer: Because the meeting ended.
exercises.hint: Check that every sentence has a main clause.

options: I was tired I went home.
I was tired, so I went home.
exercises.explanation: Two complete sentences need punctuation or a connector. Correct answer: I was tired I went home.
exercises.hint: Look for two complete ideas joined without punctuation.

exercises.prompt: Fix the fragment 'Because I was late.'
options: I apologized because I was late.
exercises.explanation: Use a period, a semicolon, or an appropriate comma and coordinating conjunction. Correct answer: I apologized because I was late.
exercises.hint: Use a connector that matches the relationship.

options: I finished the report, and I sent it.
I finished the report I sent it.
exercises.explanation: Use a period, a semicolon, or an appropriate comma and coordinating conjunction. Correct answer: I finished the report, and I sent it.
exercises.hint: Use a connector that matches the relationship.

options: The manager called, so I answered.
exercises.explanation: Use a period, a semicolon, or an appropriate comma and coordinating conjunction. Correct answer: The manager called, so I answered.
exercises.hint: Use a connector that matches the relationship.

writing.prompt: Write two related sentences and connect them correctly.
writing.exampleAnswer: I finished the report, and I sent it to my manager.

optionalSpeaking.prompt: Write two related sentences and connect them correctly.

sections.heading: Fragments
sections.explanation: A dependent clause by itself may leave an incomplete thought.
sections.example: Fragment: 'Because I was late.' Complete: 'I apologized because I was late.'

sections.heading: Run-ons
sections.explanation: Two complete sentences need punctuation or a connector.
sections.example: Run-on: 'I was tired I went home.' Correct: 'I was tired, so I went home.'

sections.heading: Joining ideas
sections.explanation: Use a period, a semicolon, or an appropriate comma and coordinating conjunction.
sections.example: The meeting ended, and we went home.

guidedSteps: Check that every sentence has a main clause.
Look for two complete ideas joined without punctuation.
Use a connector that matches the relationship.
commonMistake: 'I finished the report I sent it' needs punctuation and a connector.
